headline: In 1962 the US military proposed faking attacks on Americans to start a war with Cuba.
slides: The Joint Chiefs of Staff, the heads of the US military, signed off on a plan called Operation Northwoods.
The idea: stage attacks, blame them on Cuba, and use the outrage to justify an invasion.
Chairman Lyman Lemnitzer presented it to Defense Secretary Robert McNamara.
President Kennedy turned it down. None of it was ever carried out.
A few months later, Lemnitzer was no longer Chairman of the Joint Chiefs.
It stayed secret for 35 years. The documents were made public on November 18, 1997.
sources: Sources: Joint Chiefs of Staff memo (March 13 1962), JFK Assassination Records Review Board (1997), ABC News
